column3: The forum brings together utilities, regulators and community groups to discuss how river catchments can be managed for both people and wildlife. Sessions in Hall A focus on policy and finance, while Hall B hosts practical case studies.
Helena Marsh leads the catchment science group at the Brackenford Environment Trust. Her talk opens the forum with a view of rivers as infrastructure that serves every sector.
Samuel chairs the regional farmers network and has converted his own land to wetland grazing. He will speak about the costs and rewards of changing farm practice.
Ana studies public finance and has advised several water regulators. Her closing keynote asks who should pay for a healthy river.
· Badges must be worn at all times inside the centre.
· Wireless access is available in both halls and in the exhibition area.
· Slides from each session will be shared with registered delegates after the forum.
